title: Android Jetpack Compose
description: Beginner-to-advanced Jetpack Compose reference for composition, state, effects, layouts, lazy UI, theming, navigation, accessibility, interoperability, and performance.

sections.title: Compose Mental Model
sections.description: Describe UI from state and let the runtime update only affected parts.

subtopics.title: Composition, Recomposition & Skipping
subtopics.description: Initial composition records emitted UI. State reads create dependencies; changing observed state schedules recomposition, which may run in any order, be skipped, or be discarded.

annotations.text: Inputs describe current UI; do not mutate widgets to synchronize them.
Callbacks carry user events outward to the state owner.

callouts.title: Composable Bodies Must Be Idempotent
callouts.text: Do not start requests, write storage, navigate, or mutate external state directly during composition. Recomposition is not a lifecycle callback; use effect APIs for controlled side effects.

subtopics.title: State Reads & Recomposition Scope
subtopics.description: Read rapidly changing state as close as possible to where it is used, pass stable values, and avoid work that repeats on every recomposition.

callouts.title: derivedStateOf Has Overhead
callouts.text: Use it when inputs change more often than the derived result should invalidate UI, such as scroll position crossing a threshold. Simple string or arithmetic derivation usually belongs directly in composition.

sections.title: State, Hoisting & Screen Architecture
sections.description: Keep a single source of truth and place state at the lowest common owner that needs to control it.

subtopics.title: remember, rememberSaveable & MutableState
subtopics.description: remember retains a value across recomposition while the call remains in composition. rememberSaveable additionally restores supported small UI state after recreation.

callouts.title: remember Is Not Persistence
callouts.text: remember does not survive removal from composition or process recreation. Save small reconstruction inputs; keep application data in repositories/persistent storage.

callouts.title: Observable Collections
callouts.text: A mutableListOf inside State is not automatically observable. Publish a new immutable list or use a snapshot-aware state collection when local mutation is intentional.

subtopics.title: Stateless & Stateful Composables
subtopics.description: Hoist state by replacing internal state with a value plus event callback. This makes the UI controllable, previewable, and testable.

tabs.label: Stateless
Stateful Wrapper

callouts.title: Hoist to the Right Owner
callouts.text: Hoist screen business state to a ViewModel; keep transient element state near the element unless another component must coordinate or persist it.

subtopics.title: ViewModel, UiState & Unidirectional Data Flow
subtopics.description: A screen-level ViewModel exposes immutable state and receives user actions; the screen collects state and passes plain values/callbacks to reusable content.

callouts.title: Do Not Pass ViewModels Down the Tree
callouts.text: Pass only required state and callbacks. Reusable composables should not know navigation scope, repositories, or ViewModel implementation details.

sections.title: Side Effects & Lifecycle
sections.description: Run external work from effect APIs whose restart and cleanup behavior matches the task.

subtopics.title: LaunchedEffect, rememberCoroutineScope & SideEffect
subtopics.description: LaunchedEffect runs suspend work tied to keys; rememberCoroutineScope launches from callbacks; SideEffect publishes successful composition state to non-Compose code.

table.title: Compose Effect Selection
rows: LaunchedEffect
Run suspend work owned by composition
Starts on entry; restarts when a key changes; cancels on exit
Use stable keys that represent restart conditions
rememberCoroutineScope
Launch suspend work from an event callback
Scope survives recomposition and cancels on exit
Do not launch during composition itself
SideEffect
Publish composed state to non-Compose code
Runs after every successful recomposition
Must be fast and non-suspending
DisposableEffect
Register and unregister an observer or listener
Recreates on key change; disposes on change or exit
Always release the acquired resource in onDispose
produceState
Convert an external async source into State
Producer follows keys and composition lifetime
Conflates equal values
snapshotFlow
Observe Compose state reads as a Flow
Emits when observed snapshot values change
Collect inside a coroutine-backed effect

tabs.label: Callback Coroutine

callouts.title: Keys Define Restart Semantics
callouts.text: A changed key cancels and restarts LaunchedEffect. Missing keys use stale inputs; unstable keys restart work repeatedly. Choose keys from the identity of the work.

subtopics.title: DisposableEffect & rememberUpdatedState
subtopics.description: Use DisposableEffect for listener registration/cleanup. rememberUpdatedState lets long-lived effects call the latest callback without restarting.

callouts.title: Always Pair Registration and Disposal
callouts.text: Listeners, observers, and callbacks registered by an effect must be removed in onDispose. Empty onDispose blocks usually signal the wrong effect API.

subtopics.title: produceState & snapshotFlow
subtopics.description: produceState converts external async values into Compose State. snapshotFlow converts observable snapshot reads into a cold Flow for non-UI processing.

callouts.title: Use State for Rendering, Flow for Stream Work
callouts.text: Do not route simple UI derivation through a Flow. snapshotFlow is useful for debounce, distinctness, and non-UI reactions to snapshot changes.

sections.title: Layouts, Lazy Content & Input
sections.description: Compose constraints flow down, sizes flow up, and parents place children.

subtopics.title: Row, Column, Box & Constraints
subtopics.description: Use Row/Column for linear layout and Box for stacking. Parents provide min/max constraints; children choose a permitted size; parents place them.

callouts.title: Modifier Mechanics Are Separate
callouts.text: See Jetpack Compose Modifiers for constraint-changing order, padding, sizing, parent data, drawing, input, semantics, and custom Modifier.Node APIs.

subtopics.title: LazyColumn, LazyRow & Stable Keys
subtopics.description: Lazy containers compose visible content. Supply stable unique keys so remembered state and animations follow item identity across moves.

callouts.title: Do Not Use Index as Identity
callouts.text: When insertions or sorting occur, index keys move to different records and can transfer remembered state to the wrong item. Use durable domain IDs.

subtopics.title: Input, Focus & IME
subtopics.description: Use state-driven fields, meaningful keyboard options/actions, and explicit focus movement only where product flow requires it.

codeBlocks.code:
OutlinedTextField(
    value = email,
    onValueChange = onEmailChange,
    label = { Text("Email") },
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(
        keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email,
        imeAction = ImeAction.Next
    ),
    keyboardActions = KeyboardActions(onNext = { focusManager.moveFocus(FocusDirection.Down) }),
    isError = emailError != null,
    supportingText = { emailError?.let { Text(it) } }
)

callouts.title: Validation Is State
callouts.text: Expose clear error state and supporting text rather than relying only on color. Decide when to validate—typing, blur, or submit—based on user experience.

sections.title: Material, Theming & Adaptive UI
sections.description: Centralize design tokens and adapt structure to available space and input mode.

subtopics.title: MaterialTheme & Design Tokens
subtopics.description: Define color scheme, typography, and shapes at the app theme. Build semantic component tokens rather than scattering literal values.

callouts.title: Semantic Colors
callouts.text: Use roles such as primary, surface, onSurface, and error. Literal colors make dark theme, dynamic color, contrast, and design evolution difficult.

subtopics.title: Window Size & Adaptive Structure
subtopics.description: Respond to actual window space and posture. A phone can be wide in landscape; a desktop window can be narrow.

codeBlocks.code:
Compact width → one pane, bottom navigation
Medium width → navigation rail, optional supporting pane
Expanded width → list-detail or multi-pane
Also test: landscape, split screen, fold posture, keyboard/mouse, large fonts

callouts.title: Avoid Device-Type Branches
callouts.text: Do not infer layout solely from phone/tablet names or physical screen. Base layout decisions on current window and content requirements.

sections.title: Navigation, Accessibility & Interoperability
sections.description: Keep route boundaries small, make semantics intentional, and migrate incrementally.

subtopics.title: Navigation Boundaries
subtopics.description: Pass stable identifiers between destinations, load canonical data in the destination owner, and keep navigation operations at the screen boundary.

callouts.title: Pass IDs, Not Object Graphs
callouts.text: Navigation arguments should be small and reconstructable. Passing whole models duplicates state, risks size limits, and becomes stale after process recreation.

subtopics.title: Accessibility & Semantics
subtopics.description: Expose meaningful roles, labels, states, actions, traversal, and touch targets. Prefer built-in Material components that include baseline semantics.

callouts.title: Do Not Duplicate Speech
callouts.text: If nearby text already labels a grouped element, redundant content descriptions create noisy announcements. Merge or clear semantics deliberately and test with accessibility services.

subtopics.title: Compose/View Interoperability
subtopics.description: Use ComposeView to host Compose in Views and AndroidView to host a necessary View in Compose. Keep ownership and cleanup aligned with the host lifecycle.

callouts.title: Treat Interop as a Boundary
callouts.text: Avoid rebuilding Views in update and avoid leaking them into ViewModels. Translate state/events at the boundary and honor the embedded component's lifecycle.

sections.title: Performance, Preview & Quality Checklist
sections.description: Measure real bottlenecks and keep composables reusable, observable, and testable.

subtopics.title: Stability & Recomposition Performance
subtopics.description: Stable unchanged parameters can be skipped. Favor immutable models and measure recomposition, layout, drawing, startup, and jank before optimizing.

callouts.title: Annotations Are Contracts
callouts.text: Do not add @Stable or @Immutable to silence reports unless the type obeys the contract. Lying can prevent required recomposition and produce stale UI.

callouts.title: Collections and Stability
callouts.text: Ordinary List/Set/Map parameters may be considered unstable because mutation cannot be proven absent. Consider immutable collections or stable wrapper UI models where measurement shows value.

subtopics.title: Previews & Testable APIs
subtopics.description: Previews work best for stateless content that receives plain models and callbacks; create representative loading, empty, error, long-text, and dark-theme cases.

callouts.title: Preview Is Not Verification
callouts.text: Previews accelerate design feedback but do not replace semantics tests, screenshot checks, device behavior, or user-journey tests.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Audit state ownership, effects, identity, accessibility, adaptation, and measured performance.

codeBlocks.code:
□ UI is a deterministic function of state
□ Reusable composables receive values and callbacks
□ Screen ViewModels remain at route boundaries
□ Every effect has correct keys and cleanup
□ Lazy items use stable domain keys
□ Small UI state restores after recreation
□ Canonical data lives outside Compose
□ Loading, empty, error, offline, and retry are designed
□ Semantics, touch targets, contrast, and font scaling work
□ Compact/expanded windows and input modes work
□ Expensive work is remembered or moved out of composition
□ Stability annotations are truthful and optimization is measured
